stories.title: St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort Secures $263M Refi After Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has rescued Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company (ARTIC)’s St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort out of special servicing, supplying a $263 million loan to refinance the oceanfront property. The New York-based lender assumed $188 million in existing debt and added $70 million in new debt backing the 213-room property in Bal Harbour, Fla., north of Miami Beach, according to public mortgage documents, which valued the asset at $311 million. The new financing comes nearly a year after a $188 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan tied to the resort headed to special servicing as the financing was set to mature. Although the loan remained current and the resort maintained a debt service coverage ratio above break-even, its cash flow in 2024 was about half of 2021 levels, the year it had secured the debt. The lender, Column Financial, wanted ARTIC to buy a replacement interest rate cap, which it had yet to secure, Morningstar reported. ARTIC, which is run by a member of the Qatari ruling family, had purchased the resort for $213 million in 2014, three years after it was completed. The complex, which features three 27-story towers at 9703 Collins Avenue, houses two pools, a 14,000-square-foot spa, five dining outposts, 13,000 square feet of event space as well as a condo component. The hotel owner and condo owners have sparred. In 2024, the condo association sued ARTIC over alleged building defects, safety hazards, and financial mismanagement. The parties settled the suit a year later. Fortress Investment Group and ARTIC did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Fortress Investment Group refinances St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort, $263M loan, South Florida.
Resort cash flow in 2024 was 50% of 2021 levels; property emerged from special servicing.
CMBS loan maturity pressure and rising rate caps forced refinance despite break-even debt service.
stories.summary: Fortress rescued Al Rayyan Tourism's St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort from special servicing with a $263 million refinance, assuming $188 million in existing debt and adding $70 million in new capital. The 213-room oceanfront property in Bal Harbour, Florida—valued at $311 million—had seen cash flow decline to roughly half its 2021 peak, straining the original 2021 CMBS loan as it matured. The resort maintained adequate debt service coverage but faced pressure to secure a replacement interest rate cap, triggering the refinance.
stories.impact: South Florida hospitality distress signals tightening debt markets and pressure on mature CMBS loans with rate exposure. While this is hospitality, not multifamily, it underscores capital market stress and refinancing urgency across South Florida real estate—relevant to developers seeking to understand regional debt conditions and refinance risk for any South Florida assets in underwriting.

stories.title: First Pioneer Properties Buys Queens Retail Center for $24M
stories.excerpt: New York-based real estate management and development firm First Pioneer Properties, along with ABS Partners Real Estate, has acquired a Queens retail center from Levy Properties for $23.5 million, property records made public Thursday show. The one-story property at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside is currently home to an urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store. Jennifer Markowitz of Levy Properties signed the deal for the seller, while Suresh Sani, owner of First Pioneer Properties, signed for the buyers. ABS seems to act as a frequent co-investor and partner of First Pioneer Properties. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. The buyers and seller did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. The property has 24,000 square feet of built space and 74,350 square feet of additional air rights for a total of 98,478 buildable square feet, according to data from PincusCo. The buyers’ intentions for the property are unclear, but Queens has been awash with multifamily developments lately. This month, Wells Fargo provided a $175 million construction loan to the Domain Companies for a 429-unit mixed-income housing development at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st Street in Astoria. Also this month, LMXD and BedRock Real Estate Partners closed on a $250 million loan to build a housing development at 35-10 Steinway Street in Astoria. Earlier this summer, another Queens retail property changed hands when Punia & Marx Real Estate sold the Whitestone Shopping Center at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway for $56 million. Meanwhile, a historic Queens bowling alley — Whitestone Lanes — at 30-05 Whitestone Expressway in Flushing — sold for $45 million in June as part of a major multifamily development project coming to the area. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: First Pioneer Properties and ABS Partners acquire Queens retail center for $23.5M, Bayside.
Property has 24K built SF plus 74.35K SF air rights; total 98.48K buildable SF.
Queens experiencing robust multifamily development wave; buyers' intentions for site unclear.
stories.summary: First Pioneer Properties and ABS Partners acquired a 24,000-square-foot retail center at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside, Queens, for $23.5 million. The property, currently leased to urgent care and a children's apparel retailer, carries substantial air rights totaling nearly 75,000 additional square feet. Queens has been a hotbed of multifamily development, and the buyers' acquisition of significant air rights suggests potential residential conversion or redevelopment.
stories.impact: Retail-to-multifamily conversion signals in Queens. The large air-rights position and timing amid Queens' multifamily boom suggest this acquisition is a land play for residential. For Trammell Crow and competitors, this signals continued availability of conversion sites in Queens and validates the market's appetite for higher-density residential; monitor First Pioneer's plans to read the submarket's entitlement and financing appetite.

stories.title: Pinnacle Group Offloads $128M Condominium and Commercial Portfolio in NYC
stories.excerpt: Pinnacle Group has offloaded a $128 million residential and retail condominium portfolio in New York City, less than a year after selling off its rent-stabilized assets. The massive trade, filed in city records this week, spanned 39 transactions across Queens, Brooklyn and Manhattan. It included nearly 750 residential units, as well as dozens of retail condominiums and several parking lots. The Real Deal first reported on the sale. The buyer entities, Friar Park JW, share an address with law firm Kurzman Eisenberg Corbin & Lever. The transactions were signed by Stuart Berg, chair of the firm’s real estate practice group. A PincusCo report tied the Friar Park entities and Berg to Tremada Holdings, an affiliate of London-based property company William Pears Group. The group, through Tremada, has quietly executed bulk residential transactions across New York City over the years with Berg’s law firm, according to PincusCo. Berg, as well as spokespeople for William Pears Group and Tremada, did not respond to requests for comment. Queens-based property management company Bronstein Properties is the managing agent for the portfolio of units, according to a spokesperson for Bronstein. Pinnacle, led by Joel Wiener, made headlines in May 2025 when it placed a portfolio of roughly 5,000 rent-stabilized apartments across New York City into bankruptcy after facing approximately $574.4 million in debt. Summit Properties won the auction for the portfolio in January, paying $451.3 million for the units. The proceeds from Pinnacle’s most recent sale will pay $66 million to lender Axos Capital, TRD reported, citing filings with the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange by Pinnacle’s Israeli subsidiary Zarasai Group. Another $47 million is currently slated to be deposited into the account of Series C bondholders. A spokesperson for Pinnacle Group could not be reached for comment on the sales. bullets: Pinnacle Group offloads $128M portfolio of 750 units, 39 transactions, NYC (Queens, Brooklyn, Manhattan).
Buyer is Tremada Holdings affiliate of William Pears Group (London), via Friar Park entities.
Sale occurred less than a year after Pinnacle exited rent-stabilized assets.
stories.summary: Pinnacle Group divested a $128 million residential and retail condominium portfolio spanning 39 transactions across Queens, Brooklyn, and Manhattan, comprising nearly 750 residential units, dozens of retail condos, and parking lots. The buyer entities, Friar Park JW, are tied to Tremada Holdings, an affiliate of London-based William Pears Group, which has quietly executed multiple bulk residential transactions across New York City in recent years. The sale marks Pinnacle's rapid portfolio exit less than a year after divesting rent-stabilized assets.
stories.impact: NYC multifamily portfolio churn and foreign capital interest. Pinnacle's rapid asset exit suggests a developer or operator recalibrating its NYC exposure—likely due to rent regulation and operational complexity. William Pears/Tremada's acquisition signals international capital remains interested in NYC multifamily at scale, but Pinnacle's retreat indicates margin pressure or strategic shift. For TCR, this confirms NYC portfolio consolidation ongoing and highlights that institutional foreign capital is acquiring bulk portfolios at perceived discounts.

stories.title: PACE Loan Group Adds CRE Vet Kenneth Sacco as CFO
stories.excerpt: PACE Loan Group (PLG) has hired a commercial real estate veteran and finance leader to shepherd its capital markets momentum in the growing commercial property assessed clean energy (C-PACE) market. The Minneapolis-based lender named Kenneth Sacco, who has advised on more than $10 billion worth of transactions and executed over $30 billion in debt financings in his CRE career, as its new chief financial officer Friday, Commercial Observer can first report. As PLG scales, that combination is exactly what we need to build out our finance and capital markets function.” Sacco began his finance career as a management consultant in the real estate advisory practices of Ernst & Young and KPMG before moving into investment banking roles at Lehman Brothers in New York and Barclays Capital in London. He later worked on the brokerage side of the CRE business as a managing director leading financial advisory practices at CBRE and JLL. bullets: PACE Loan Group hires Kenneth Sacco as CFO; Sacco has $30B+ debt financing experience in CRE.
Sacco previously held senior finance roles at Netflix and Life Time; marks CRE return.
Move aims to scale PLG's capital markets function in growing C-PACE lending market.
stories.summary: PACE Loan Group, a Minneapolis-based lender, hired CRE finance veteran Kenneth Sacco as chief financial officer to guide growth in the commercial property assessed clean energy (C-PACE) financing market. Sacco brings over $30 billion in debt financing execution and $10 billion in transaction advisory across his CRE career, plus recent senior finance experience at Netflix and Life Time. The hire signals PLG's confidence in C-PACE market expansion and intent to scale institutional capital markets capabilities.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. C-PACE financing is a niche energy-efficiency/retrofit capital source, not core construction or permanent debt for new multifamily builds. However, Sacco's hire may indicate growing appetite from institutional capital for sustainable and energy-efficient residential projects; developers with LEED/Passive House aspirations should consider C-PACE as a complementary financing layer for retrofits or high-efficiency new construction.

stories.title: Office, Industrial Occupancy Rates Edge Up in The Woodlands
stories.excerpt: Vacancy rates in The Woodlands area grew slightly in retail and industrial sectors in August, while the office sector saw a slight decrease when compared to the third quarter of 2025, according to commercial real estate data from Caldwell Cos. Community Impact reports that rental rates per square foot for retail units grew between the third quarter of 2025 and early August, by $3.70 per square foot. Office units in the Woodlands area saw a $1.96 per square foot increase in monthly leasing rates in the same period. Industrial units follow the same trend of slow increases since the third quarter of 2023. New construction for the industrial sector has slowed in both new buildings and square footage since the third quarter of 2025, with 14 buildings underway as of Aug. 4 compared to 30 about a year ago. Retail sector construction is down slightly in the same time period. The post Office, Industrial Occupancy Rates Edge Up in The Woodlands appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: The Woodlands, Texas: retail rents up $3.70/SF, office up $1.96/SF since Q3 2025.
Industrial new construction halted; 14 buildings underway vs. 30 a year ago.
Office occupancy edged up slightly; retail and industrial vacancy grew marginally.
stories.summary: The Woodlands, Texas, commercial market showed mixed signals in early August 2025: retail rents rose $3.70 per square foot and office rents climbed $1.96 per square foot since Q3 2025, while office occupancy edged up. However, industrial new construction collapsed, with only 14 buildings underway as of August 4, down from 30 about a year prior. Retail construction also slowed, and retail and industrial vacancy rates ticked up slightly.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily. The Woodlands data reflects Houston-area industrial and retail dynamics, not residential demand signals. However, if industrial development is cooling in The Woodlands, it may signal slower population/job inflows into the outer Houston ring, which could dampen long-term multifamily demand in suburban Houston submarkets—worth monitoring for impact on The Woodlands and adjacent residential markets if trend persists.

stories.title: Nominations Are Open for Connect CRE’s 2026 Women in Real Estate Awards
stories.excerpt: Nominations are open for the 10th consecutive year of Connect CRE’s Women in Real Estate Awards. We will honor women whose talent, drive, leadership and fresh ideas have helped them succeed and become influential in commercial real estate. We invite you to participate in selecting this year’s honorees. We’ll put the spotlight on women from each of the 11 regions we cover with daily news. From coast to coast, that means honorees from California; Seattle and the Pacific Northwest; Phoenix and the Southwest; Texas; Chicago and the Midwest; Boston and New England; New York and Tri-State; Washington, DC; Atlanta and the Southeast; and Florida and the Gulf Coast, as well as National honorees.  Along with nominees from across the country, we’re also looking across the CRE spectrum. After considering your recommendations, we’ll choose this year’s honorees. We’ll begin announcing them in October. The deadline for nominations is Friday, Sept. 11. bullets: Connect CRE announces 2026 Women in Real Estate Awards; 10th consecutive year.
Nominations open across 11 regional markets and multiple CRE disciplines.
Honorees to be announced in October 2026; awards span brokerage, finance, development, law.
stories.summary: Connect CRE opened nominations for its 10th consecutive Women in Real Estate Awards, recognizing women leaders across 11 U.S. regions and multiple CRE disciplines including brokerage, finance, development, investment, asset management, and real estate law. Honorees will be announced beginning in October 2026.
stories.impact: No direct impact to multifamily development. This is an industry recognition program announcement and carries no market signal on demand, supply, capital, or cost.

stories.title: Varia US, Brookfield Launch $694M Multifamily Joint Venture
stories.excerpt: Varia US Properties AG, the Swiss-listed investor in the U.S. multifamily sector, externally managed by Stoneweg, an SWI Group Company, has formed a US$693.9 million two-vehicle joint venture with affiliates of Brookfield Asset Management for 13 of Varia’s 17-property U.S. multifamily portfolio. The JV provides access to up to US$200 million equity capital to fund future acquisitions, enabling Varia US to expand its portfolio and reposition the Company towards a higher-quality portfolio. Varia US will actively invest in the JV assets to maximize value ahead of planned disposals. Comprising 4,112 units across nine U.S. states, the 13 properties have been divided into two newly formed vehicles, with an aggregate gross asset value of approximately $694 million. Four properties will remain wholly owned and consolidated by Varia US. Max-Herve George, co-founder and CEO of SWI Group, said, “This joint venture gives us the firepower and the flexibility to concentrate on high-quality residential communities, while positioning Varia US to grow decisively as the U.S. living sector continues to reward scale and discipline.” Pictured: Varia US’ Rolling Hills Apartments in Louisville, KY. Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Gain firsthand insights from industry leaders on capital markets, development, operations, financing, and investment trends while expanding your network with the people making deals happen. See you on September 22! The post Varia US, Brookfield Launch $694M Multifamily Joint Venture appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Varia US and Brookfield launch $694M JV for 13 of 17 multifamily properties; 4,112 units.
JV provides access to $200M equity capital for future acquisitions and repositioning.
Properties span nine U.S. states; four remaining properties stay wholly owned by Varia US.
stories.summary: Swiss-listed multifamily investor Varia US Properties AG, managed by Stoneweg, partnered with Brookfield Asset Management affiliates to form a $693.9 million joint venture covering 13 of its 17 U.S. multifamily properties, totaling 4,112 units across nine states. The JV provides access to up to $200 million in equity capital to fund future acquisitions and reposition toward higher-quality assets. Four properties remain wholly owned by Varia US, and the company plans to actively invest in the JV portfolio ahead of planned disposals.
stories.impact: Institutional capital aggregation and portfolio repositioning in multifamily. Varia's JV with Brookfield signals a shift toward quality over quantity and suggests that second-tier multifamily operators (especially those with offshore capital structures) are consolidating and levering their balance sheets to acquire higher-quality assets. The $200M equity commitment reflects continued institutional confidence in multifamily; for TCR, this validates that capital is flowing to scale operators willing to reposition. Monitor Varia/Brookfield disposals for potential acquisition targets and insight into which markets/assets are being exited.

stories.title: Logistics Plus Signs 744K-SF Wilmer Warehouse Lease
stories.excerpt: Logistics Plus has signed a 744,452-square-foot industrial lease in the southern Dallas suburb of Wilmer. The Pennsylvania-based provider of freight and fulfillment services will occupy the entire Building 2 within the Southport Logistics Center, an approximately 1.5 million-square-foot development. Building 2 features 123 dock doors, three drive-in doors and 4,647 square feet of speculative office space. Building 1, still vacant, includes 121 dock doors, four drive-in doors, 389 car parking spaces, 170 trailer parking spaces, and 3,534 square feet of speculative office space. Kurt Griffin and Nathan Orbin of JLL represented the landlord, a joint venture between Bandera Ventures and Invesco Real Estate, in the lease negotiations. In addition to the Wilmer site, Logistics Plus has another warehouse in Haslet. The facilities have a combined 2 million square feet of storage space in the region. Logistics Plus has over 12 million square feet of commercial warehouse space across North America. The post Logistics Plus Signs 744K-SF Wilmer Warehouse Lease appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Logistics Plus signs 744.5K-SF lease, Building 2, Southport Logistics Center, Wilmer, Dallas.
Tenant occupies entire building with 123 dock doors; combined 2M SF Dallas-area footprint.
Logistics Plus operates 12M+ SF nationally; JV developer is Bandera Ventures and Invesco.
stories.summary: Logistics Plus, a Pennsylvania-based freight and fulfillment provider, leased the entire 744,452-square-foot Building 2 at Southport Logistics Center in Wilmer, south of Dallas. The building features 123 dock doors and serves as part of Logistics Plus's expanding Dallas-area presence, bringing its local footprint to 2 million square feet. The development is a joint venture between Bandera Ventures and Invesco Real Estate.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. Large industrial leasing in southern Dallas reflects ongoing logistics and e-commerce demand in the region, not residential. However, strong industrial absorption in Wilmer and Dallas validates population and job growth in the southern Dallas corridor, which indirectly supports multifamily demand in adjacent residential submarkets. If industrial tenants are expanding footprints in Wilmer, working-age population and wage growth will follow, supporting multifamily rent growth and occupancy in nearby communities.

stories.title: Data Center Supplier Inks 196K-SF Lease in Hutto
stories.excerpt: Partners Real Estate represented AI Prefab Solutions, a Texas-based critical-infrastructure manufacturer, in its lease of a new 196,523-sq.-ft. Class A facility in Hutto, Texas. The facility, known as Innovation 8, stretches just under three football fields in length and will serve as the company’s headquarters and primary manufacturing site, with its first system entering production in September 2026. Partners Real Estate’s Stan Nowak and Andrew Alizzi led the assignment on behalf of AI Prefab Solutions, which designs, builds, integrates, and factory-tests prefabricated modular power solutions that bring hyperscale data centers and semiconductor facilities online faster, safer, and more reliably. Innovation Business Park is a Hutto industrial development anchored by major corporate neighbors and expanding infrastructure. Demand for advanced manufacturing and critical infrastructure space has grown alongside the AI compute buildout across Central Texas, where well-located industrial product remains in short supply. AI Prefab Solutions plans to add 200 to 300 full-time employees by 2028. The post Data Center Supplier Inks 196K-SF Lease in Hutto appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: AI Prefab Solutions leases 196.5K-SF facility in Hutto, Texas; critical-infrastructure manufacturing HQ.
Company plans to hire 200–300 FTEs by 2028; first production starts September 2026.
Demand for advanced manufacturing and critical-infrastructure space surging alongside AI compute buildup in Central Texas.
stories.summary: AI Prefab Solutions, a Texas-based critical-infrastructure manufacturer, leased a new 196,523-square-foot Class A facility in Hutto, Texas, to serve as its headquarters and primary manufacturing site. The company designs and builds prefabricated power solutions for hyperscale data centers and semiconductor facilities. AI Prefab plans to add 200–300 full-time employees by 2028, with first production beginning in September 2026. Demand for advanced manufacturing space in Central Texas is accelerating alongside the region's AI compute and semiconductor expansion.
stories.impact: Strong indirect multifamily demand signal for Central Texas, especially Hutto. AI Prefab's 200–300 FTE addition to Hutto, combined with the region's data center and semiconductor buildout, will drive strong population and wage growth in the Austin-Hutto corridor. This validates multifamily acquisition and development opportunity in Hutto and northern Austin submarkets ahead of the 2026–2028 employment wave. Developers should prioritize Hutto and I-35 North Austin for mid-to-high density product; industrial/manufacturing job adds historically precede strong residential demand.

stories.title: S3 Capital Lends $35M for Miami-Dade County Apartments
stories.excerpt: Miami developer Aconcagua Group has landed $35 million of construction financing to complete a multifamily project in Miami-Dade County, Commercial Observer has learned. S3 Capital provided the loan for the third and final phase of the 374-unit Casa Princeton apartment community in Princeton, Fla. The deal closed Friday morning. The phase three portion of the development will comprise an eight-story building with 162 apartments. The second phase Casa Princeton, encompassing 150 units, was delivered in March 2026 and is roughly 40 percent leased, according to S3. “Casa Princeton speaks directly to the attainable housing gap we’re seeing in markets across Florida,” Steven Jemal, managing director of origination at S3 Capital, said in a statement. “The absorption of the initial phases has validated the underlying demand for the product, which gives us conviction as a lender.” Berkadia negotiated the debt with a Miami-based team consisting of Charles Foschini and Christopher Apone. Located at 12835 SW 246th Terrace 30 miles south of Downtown Miami, the apartment community features one and two-bedroom floorplans. Community amenities include a clubhouse, event space, co-working areas, swimming pool, fitness center, playground and dog park. “The Live Local program is a practical example of public policy helping experienced developers deliver more housing where it is needed,” Robert Schwartz, managing principal at S3 Capital, said in a statement. “We’re proud to participate in public-private partnership programs like this, which make it economically possible to increase limited housing supplies and generate value for local communities, developers and our own stakeholders.” Aconcagua Group did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: S3 Capital provides $35M construction financing for Casa Princeton Phase 3, Miami-Dade County.
Phase 3 adds 162 units (8-story building); total project is 374 units; Phase 2 (150 units) 40% leased as of March 2026.
S3 Capital highlights attainable housing demand gap validated by Phase 2 absorption.
stories.summary: Miami-based Aconcagua Group closed a $35 million construction loan from S3 Capital to complete the third phase of the Casa Princeton apartment community in Princeton, Florida (Miami-Dade County). Phase 3 will add 162 units in an eight-story building, bringing the total project to 374 units. Phase 2, delivered in March 2026 with 150 units, had achieved roughly 40 percent occupancy at the time of Phase 3 financing, validating strong underlying demand for workforce/attainable housing in the market.
stories.impact: South Florida attainable-housing demand validated. Phase 2's 40% absorption in three months signals strong demand for workforce apartments in Miami-Dade County, confirming that multifamily developers have a viable path to lender support for Class B/C product in Miami-Dade. For TCR, this suggests a capital window for attainable housing in South Florida before rates compress further; lenders like S3 are actively deploying construction capital into workforce product, indicating conviction in the segment's durability. Monitor Casa Princeton's Phase 2–3 performance for rent velocity and lease-up pace as a bellwether for Miami-Dade market health and underwriting calibration.
